chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَمْرُو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ

translations.en: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah narrated from his father from his grandfather from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi from his father from Amr ibn Shimmer from Abdullah who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ الصَّادِقُ ع: مَنْ أَقَرَّ بِسِتَّةِ أَشْيَاءَ فَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ: الْبَرَاءَةِ مِنَ الطَّوَغِيتِ، وَالْإِقْرَارِ بِالْوِلَايَةِ، وَالْإِيمَانِ وَالِاسْتِحْلَالِ لِلْمُتْعَةِ، وَتَحْرِيمِ الْجِرِّيِّ، وَتَرْكِ الْمَسْحِ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ.

translations.en: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: He who acknowledges six things is a believer: Disavowal of the Taghut, declaration of Wilayah (guardianship), belief in Rajaa (return), legality of Mut'ah (temporary marriage), prohibition of the Eel (Jirri), and leaving off wiping over the Khuff (leather socks).

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates six pillars that distinguish the Shia identity, blending core theological convictions with distinct jurisprudential practices. This hadith highlights the integration of faith (Iman) with specific legal markers, such as the permissibility of Mut'ah and the rejection of wiping over leather socks (Al-Khuffayn), which serve as practical identifiers of the school. These criteria underscore the Shia emphasis on both doctrinal purity and adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's specific interpretation of Islamic law.
en.seo_question: What are the six essential beliefs and practices that define a Shia Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?

key_terms.الطَّوَغِيتِ: Taghut (idols, tyrants, or anything worshipped besides God)
key_terms.الْجِرِّيِّ: Al-Jirri (a type of eel, specifically its flesh)
key_terms.الْخُفَّيْنِ: Al-Khuffayn (the pair of leather socks worn for wiping during ablution)
